note: Curated Vahana Labs editorial layer. Routine ingestion never writes to this file. Each entry is keyed by question id. 'tension' is rendered only when the live data for that question meets the evidence threshold in scripts/pipeline/taxonomies.py. 'vahana_read' fields are optional; only fields with content are shown.

groups.label: Manufacturers
groups.text: Accept risk-based tiering; resist variability itself being treated as a hazard.

groups.label: Health systems
groups.text: Accept the frame but say it fails where a tool shifts behavior mid-conversation.

groups.label: Researchers
groups.text: Want risk expressed distributionally, including tail behavior.

tension.synthesis: There is broad agreement on risk-based tiering. The disagreement is about what gets measured: manufacturers want consequence of action, health systems want behavior over a session, researchers want the shape of the output distribution.

vahana_read.alignment: No commenter argues for a uniform evidence bar. Proportionality is settled.
vahana_read.tension: The unit of analysis is unsettled: output, session, or deployment.
vahana_read.missing: Intended use may need to be described as a behavioral envelope with defined exit conditions, rather than a static statement.

groups.label: Manufacturers
groups.text: Accept a high bar if it is stated in advance.

groups.label: Professional societies
groups.text: Want prospective, in-setting evidence for anything that informs a decision.

groups.label: Trade associations
groups.text: Warn that a prospective floor prices out low-risk tools.

tension.synthesis: Nobody argues against proportionality. The dispute is where the prospective-evidence line sits, and whether the cost of clearing it falls on tools whose harm potential is mainly operational.

vahana_read.alignment: Predictability is valued more than leniency across all four stakeholder groups.
vahana_read.tension: Prospective evidence for mid-tier tools is the live fault line.
vahana_read.commercialization: If prospective or continuously refreshed clinical evidence becomes expected across broader risk tiers, some lower-value GenAI use cases may no longer support viable economics. Evidence expectations feed development capital, time to market, and the minimum contract value a product needs to justify itself.
vahana_read.deployment: Buyers will ask which tier a product sits in and what evidence travels with it. Vendors without an evidence package a health system can drop into its own review absorb that work inside the sales cycle.
vahana_read.missing: Evidence economics: if continuous validation is required at every tier, the obligations may become unscalable before they become unsafe.

groups.label: Professional societies
groups.text: Want the combined system evaluated, with override behavior measured.

groups.label: Manufacturers
groups.text: Accept the concept, resist accountability for site-level variation.

groups.label: Patient groups
groups.text: Question whether the proposed metrics measure safety at all.

tension.synthesis: All three groups accept that model-only performance is insufficient. The unresolved question is who is accountable for the part of the system that lives inside a hospital.

vahana_read.alignment: Model-only metrics are widely treated as inadequate.
vahana_read.tension: Accountability for the human half of the system.
vahana_read.commercialization: If claims must cover the clinician-plus-tool system, training, workflow design, and oversight tooling stop being services around the product and become part of it. That changes what is built, what is priced, and what a competitor has to reproduce.
vahana_read.deployment: Sites may need defined oversight expectations, override monitoring, and training fidelity at go-live, and contracts may need to say who is accountable when local practice differs from the evaluated conditions.
vahana_read.missing: Human-AI system performance may need its own reporting construct rather than being folded into human factors.

vahana_read.commercialization: A premarket-for-postmarket trade lowers the cost of getting to market and raises the cost of staying there. Products that can fund a durable monitoring program gain time to market; products that cannot inherit an obligation their margin was never built to carry.
vahana_read.deployment: If reduced premarket evidence is justified by monitoring, the monitoring has to actually run at the site. Health systems become part of the evidence base whether or not their contracts say so.

groups.label: Manufacturers and trade associations
groups.text: Accept the duty; want a scalable, sampling-based framework.

groups.label: Health systems
groups.text: Support monitoring but resist absorbing manufacturer surveillance obligations.

groups.label: AI companies
groups.text: Focus on the data pathway that makes monitoring technically possible.

tension.synthesis: Every group supports monitoring and every group locates the operating burden somewhere else. The unsettled question is not whether to monitor but who pays for the part that happens inside the hospital.

vahana_read.alignment: No commenter opposes postmarket monitoring in principle.
vahana_read.tension: Cost and labor allocation between manufacturer and site.
vahana_read.commercialization: Monitoring obligations become an operating cost inside the product's margin. If the vendor does not fund site-level surveillance, the cost is either priced into the contract or quietly transferred to the customer.
vahana_read.deployment: Contracts may need to define telemetry access, monitoring responsibility, escalation pathways, and who bears the operational cost. Without that, monitoring exists on paper at every site and in practice at none.
vahana_read.missing: Distributed accountability: the parties who can detect a problem, diagnose it, and fix it are three different organizations.

groups.label: Manufacturers
groups.text: Want change control extended to changes they do not control.

groups.label: AI companies
groups.text: Point to commercial deprecation timelines that regulation has not accounted for.

groups.label: Health systems
groups.text: Want notification before behavior changes reach clinicians.

tension.synthesis: The parties agree that current change control assumes a version cadence generative products do not have. They differ on whether the fix belongs in the sponsor's PCCP or in supplier obligations.

vahana_read.alignment: Predetermined change control is accepted as the right instrument.
vahana_read.tension: Whether supplier-initiated change belongs inside the sponsor's plan.
vahana_read.commercialization: If sponsors must revalidate after upstream foundation-model changes, model dependency becomes more than a technical decision. It becomes a switching-cost, regulatory-risk, and financing consideration.
vahana_read.deployment: Sites may need a change-management process for updates they did not schedule: advance notice, a local check before behavior-changing releases reach clinicians, and a documented rollback path.
vahana_read.missing: AI supplier quality: foundation model providers now behave like critical suppliers whose release schedules can alter regulated product behavior.

groups.label: Health systems
groups.text: Want a defined local validation step and are willing to run it.

groups.label: Manufacturers
groups.text: Will define a supported envelope; resist owning site deviations.

groups.label: Researchers
groups.text: Note that the measurement infrastructure does not exist yet.

tension.synthesis: There is no disagreement that deployment changes behavior. The gap is that no party currently owns, funds, or can observe performance at the site level.

vahana_read.alignment: Deployment-specific variation is treated as real by every group that raised it.
vahana_read.tension: Who validates, and against what baseline.
vahana_read.commercialization: If assurance is partly local, implementation stops being a cost center and becomes part of the offer. A repeatable deployment-assurance package shortens sales cycles and adds defensibility; its absence caps how many sites can be run at once.
vahana_read.deployment: FDA clearance may not eliminate the need for local validation. Health systems may need defined go-live and revalidation processes covering configuration, population, workflow, and model change.
vahana_read.missing: Deployment-specific assurance is largely absent from the paper, though it is where most reported behavior differences originate.

groups.label: Trade associations
groups.text: Extend existing supplier controls rather than write new ones.

groups.label: AI companies
groups.text: Accept notification duties, resist training-data transparency.

groups.label: Manufacturers
groups.text: Want contractual visibility to match regulatory liability.

tension.synthesis: All parties accept that foundation model providers sit inside the safety system. They differ on how much of the supplier's internals the sponsor is entitled to see.

vahana_read.alignment: Supplier framing is accepted by suppliers themselves.
vahana_read.tension: Depth of disclosure versus sufficiency of notification.
vahana_read.commercialization: Supplier obligations shape build-versus-depend decisions. Change notice, version pinning, and re-verification capacity become diligence questions for investors and buyers, not engineering preferences.
vahana_read.deployment: Vendors may need a re-verification test bed and a notification chain that reaches deployed sites, since a supplier release can change clinician-visible behavior with no local action at all.
vahana_read.missing: Notification without re-verification capacity does not protect a patient; the sponsor needs time and a test bed, not only a message.

groups.label: Professional societies
groups.text: Focus on intervention points before execution.

groups.label: AI companies
groups.text: Focus on declaring permitted actions in labeling.

groups.label: Health systems
groups.text: Focus on who inside the organization actually delegated the authority.

tension.synthesis: The three groups describe the same problem at three different layers: the moment of execution, the product's declared scope, and the organizational decision to switch a capability on.

vahana_read.alignment: Action-taking systems are treated as categorically different from text-producing ones.
vahana_read.tension: Whether control belongs in the product, the labeling, or site governance.
vahana_read.commercialization: Action-taking products carry a higher assurance burden and a higher contract value, because they remove work rather than draft it. The economics turn on how much authority a customer will actually delegate.
vahana_read.deployment: Organizations may need an explicit delegation record: which actions are enabled, who approved them, where a human intervenes, and how far an error can travel before anyone notices.
vahana_read.missing: Delegated authority: how far an error can propagate before meaningful human intervention may be the defining measure for agentic systems.
